The detected absorption line at 3.9 µeV from a source at 2.1 Gpc corresponds to a redshifted 21 cm line (rest energy ~5.9 µeV). The 21 cm line arises from the hyperfine transition of neutral atomic hydrogen (HI). In the Milky Way, this absorption line is most commonly associated with the cold atomic interstellar medium, where cool, dense HI clouds produce narrow absorption features against background radio sources. Warm atomic gas typically produces emission, while molecular gas is traced by other lines (e.g., CO).
